title: Intent versus permission
intro: An instruction says what an agent should do. Authorization determines whether its identity is allowed to perform the requested operation on the resource.
takeaway: Enforce important boundaries in the application or service. A persistent instruction cannot replace an authorization check.

beats.text: The agent is told not to deploy. That instruction expresses the policy.
Suppose it still requests deployment. The service must check its identity.
This identity has no deploy permission. Authorization rejects the operation.
The deploy service is never invoked. Enforce access outside the model.

title: Grant only needed access
intro: An incident investigation needs access to particular service logs. Give the investigating identity only the operations and resources required.
takeaway: Least privilege applies to both action and resource. A read capability should not implicitly grant deployment or unrelated data access.

beats.text: The agent needs checkout service logs. Its identity is allowed to read that scope.
The service checks this read request. Permission applies to action and resource.
The approved read is executed. The permitted logs can be returned.
A read of payments logs is different. This identity lacks that permission.

title: Policy and permission
intro: Guardrails can include deterministic validation and model-based judgments. Their reliability differs. Authorization should still be checked for every execution.
takeaway: A guardrail pass is not a security guarantee. Keep identity-based permission enforcement at the action boundary.

beats.text: A proposed action enters a policy check. Some checks involve fallible judgments.
The policy check accepts the proposal. That result alone does not grant access.
Authorization still checks the operation. The identity lacks the required permission.
Do not execute the unauthorized action. A guardrail pass cannot override this check.

title: Review a concrete action
intro: The agent can propose a release without holding production credentials. A reviewer checks the exact artifact, target and supporting evidence.
takeaway: Approval must refer to the action actually executed. A separate executor enforces that binding.

beats.text: The agent prepares release r42. Its proposal names the production target.
Send the artifact and test evidence. The reviewer can inspect a concrete action.
The reviewer approves that exact release. The executor checks artifact and target.
Only the authorized action proceeds. The agent itself stays read-only.

title: Recheck changed actions
intro: An approval for r42 does not authorize a later r43 artifact. The executor compares the current action with the approved one.
takeaway: Bind authorization to significant action data and recheck it at execution time. Changed intent requires a new decision.

beats.text: The saved approval names release r42. The proposed artifact is now r43.
The executor receives the new proposal. It checks the stored approval.
The artifact identifiers do not match. The executor blocks the changed action.
Get review for the actual new artifact. Do not reuse approval for different work.
